smell_validity.evidence: Eight publishing stages each hold private complete declarations of the same roster in varied shapes — arrays, infix tables, a membership gate, a switch — while the shared locales.ts still exports roster and naming. One conceptual change genuinely forces a scattered trail of coordinated edits: the classic shotgun-surgery weakness, clearly and consequentially exposed.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Adding or renaming a language now requires finding and editing eight scattered, structurally different copies; a missed one silently drops routes, READMEs, menu entries or translations. Removing the scatter restores a single ownership boundary, making future work safer, not just shorter. Slightly below architecture-level, but a lasting maintenance trap.

development_plausibility.evidence: Each copy fits its stage's local idiom — route constants beside build(), a menu list, function-local disk-suffix tables, a switch when 'which language' replaces 'default vs rest'. Comments record local assumptions and behavior is preserved. Minor artificial regularity: eight simultaneous copies and near-identical five-entry tables.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: The prompt names the diagnosis, names every stage-level copy pattern, defines the finished state (stages consume shared locales.ts; no private enumeration), and sharply bounds preservation: exact naming interpolation for unknown codes, byte-identical artifacts, untouched language set and corpus, other callers still compiling. This decisively prevents wrong direction and irrelevant redesign.

semantic_diversity.evidence: At least four purposes: iteration/emission (build), name formation (toUrl, readme, translate, resolve), membership gating (formatToCode), and menu selection (generate-play). Several need different decisions — preserving existence checks and fallbacks in URL builders versus plain infix lookup versus gating — though some collapse into one shared naming rule.

localization_burden.evidence: The maintainer observation names every affected stage, but sites hide in varied forms: two arrays, four infix tables at different scopes, a gate, a switch, plus casts and fallback interpolations. The complete scope is effectively listed, so discovery burden is modest; verifying each copy still requires reading each stage's use.

repair_coordination.evidence: All sites must adopt one shared roster and naming rule; if a stage keeps its copy or drops the existence-check combined into publishedReadmeName calls, artifacts silently diverge. Changes at each location must agree with the shared module's restored shape, but most follow one reconnection rule without interacting rules.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: A uniform fix — import supportedLocales/f and delete local copies — covers the array and table sites in build, generate-play, readme, translate, loader (roughly five of eight), but cannot uniformly handle the switch in resolve.ts, the gate in formatToCode, or the fallback-preserving URL builders; those require separate judgment.

behavioral_risk.evidence: A plausible wrong edit — reconnecting name formation without preserving existence checks or unknown-code fallback — compiles and produces ordinary URLs/paths, but silently breaks localized links for missing translations or unknown codes; only special states reveal it. No test evidence in the supplied material shows these paths checked.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
